prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Houston. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Houston for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I’ll need one quick detail to give specific names and phone numbers: what ZIP code or neighborhood in Houston are you closest to (or do you prefer a particular area of town)?

Meanwhile, here’s a concise plan and the kinds of practices you should call right now, and why each type is useful. This will help you compare options when I pull specific offices for your area.

Which practices to call (by type) and why
- Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeons (OMS)
  - Why: Specialists in the surgical placement of implants and complex extractions, bone grafting, sinus lifts, and sedation/general anesthesia. Best if you have significant bone loss, impacted teeth, or medical/health concerns.
- Periodontists
  - Why: Specialists in the gums and supporting bone; they commonly place implants and manage gum disease and grafts around implants. Good for focused implant work and periodontal health.
- Prosthodontists
  - Why: Specialists in restoring teeth (crowns, bridges, complex implant-supported dentures). If your case requires a highly cosmetic or technically complex prosthesis, call a prosthodontist for the restorative phase (or a team that includes one).
- Multi‑disciplinary implant centers / full‑service implant practices
  - Why: These coordinate surgery and restoration in-house (OMS/periodontist + prosthodontist), which simplifies communication and scheduling. Good for full‑arch reconstructions or streamlined care.
- Academic dental clinics (UTHealth School of Dentistry)
  - Why: Faculty-supervised specialists-in-training often provide advanced care at lower cost; good option if cost is an issue and you’re comfortable with a teaching environment.

What to ask when you call (quick checklist)
- Do you place dental implants? If so, which specialists (OMS / perio / prostho)?
- How many implants do you place per year (or per doctor) and what implant systems do you use?
- Do you do CBCT 3D imaging in-office and is it included in the consult?
- Will the same office do the final crown/bridge/denture or will I be referred out?
- Do you offer sedation or IV anesthesia and do you have hospital privileges if needed?
- What’s the estimated cost range for a single implant (implant + abutment + crown) and are CT, grafts, or temporary teeth included?
- Do you provide a written treatment plan, timeline, and warranty/guarantee on the implant/restoration?
- Do you accept my insurance or offer financing/third‑party plans?

How to choose between offices
- Choose an OMS or periodontist for surgical complexity (bone grafts, sinus lifts).
- Choose a prosthodontist or a team-based center for complex restorations or esthetics.
- Look for in‑office CBCT, digital planning (guided surgery), and case photos/reviews.
- Confirm board certification and membership in professional bodies (AAOMS, AAP, AAID, ACP).
- Read recent patient reviews and ask to see before/after photos of cases like yours.

If you want, I will:
- Look up 3–5 specific practices within your ZIP code or neighborhood (OMS, perio, prostho, and a university option), include phone numbers, one-sentence reason to call each, and any notes about insurance/financing. Just tell me your ZIP code or area and any preferences (insurance, budget, timeline, single tooth vs full arch).
